name: same-file-reads
means: An anchor's fingerprint covers its extent from its first attachment and, transitively, the same-file declarations and import bindings it reads, so changing any of them stales the relations confirmed on that fingerprint (a relation whose seen is in an older format is the exception staleness-against-seen states). What is hashed is normalized by file kind: for Python that tokenizes, the case the related test exercises, it is the token sequence with comments, blank lines and line ends dropped, so a comment, a blank line, spacing between tokens within a line, or a line break inside brackets changes nothing, while every token's own text counts — an indentation's whitespace, a name, a string literal's quotes and contents — and so does a line break that opens or closes an indented block, which adds or removes indentation tokens; Python that does not tokenize is hashed as its text, and a Markdown section as its text without trailing blank lines, so a comment or spacing change there counts; other kinds' rules are not claimed here. What an anchor reads in another file is not followed and has to be related on its own.
